title: Do “Made in USA” Claims Matter?
eligible_reason: Single adoption date in every DiD. Each column of Tables 4 (HMS) and 5 (RMS) compares ONE focal brand that stopped making 'Made in USA' claims after a single FTC closing-letter date (Gorilla glue 2015-06-05, Loctite 2015-09-18, Gorilla tape 2015-06-05, Tramontina cookware 2015-11-13) with 2-4 never-treated control brands over a +/-8-week window (w8==1). treat = 1[after==1 & brand==focal] is a classic two-group, single-date DiD, so the at-least-two-adoption-cohorts rule fails. Panel B columns add time-varying ad-duration and price-index controls. The eBay results (Tables 8-11) are a randomized field experiment, not a DiD.
design_notes: HMS (8_DID_hms.R): brand-week national panel of log Nielsen Homescan sales; felm(logsales ~ treat | brand_descr + week_end), no clustering, 3-4 brands per regression. RMS (9_DID_rms.R): brand-store-week panel of log(sales+1); felm(... | brand_descr:store_code_uc + store_code_uc:week_end | 0 | store_code_uc), i.e. brand-by-store FE and store-by-week FE, clustered by store. 'after' = week_end >= first Saturday after the FTC date (mark12Week in 3_prep_hms_sales.ipynb / 4_prep_rms_sales.ipynb). One treated brand per regression; the date differs across regressions but each regression has one cohort. The 'two-way fixed effects' and 'difference-in-differences' hits refer to these two-group designs.
estimators_reported: TWFE two-group static DiD (lfe::felm), Tables 4-5 Panels A-B
OLS on randomized eBay auction experiment (Tables 8-10)
n_adoption_cohorts_note: One treated brand and one FTC date per regression (four separate single-date DiDs).
